name: Tawang Monastery (Galden Namgyal Lhatse)
description: Largest Buddhist monastery in India and second-largest in the world, belonging to the Gelug school. Founded in 1680-81 by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso on the wishes of the 5th Dalai Lama. Features an 8-metre gilded Buddha statue, ancient scriptures, and panoramic views of the Tawang Chu valley. Birthplace connection to the 6th Dalai Lama.
facts: Founded 1680-81 by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso

name: Tawang Town
description: District headquarters and main tourist base in Tawang district at about 3,000 m elevation. Gateway for exploring the monastery, lakes, and high-altitude sites. Known for Monpa culture, handicrafts, and markets.
facts: Base for Bum La and Madhuri Lake trips

name: Urgelling Monastery
description: Historic Buddhist monastery and birthplace of the 6th Dalai Lama Tsangyang Gyatso (born 1683). Founded around 1489 by Urgen Sangpo. Smaller and quieter than Tawang Monastery, with traditional Tibetan architecture and spiritual significance for pilgrims.
facts: Birthplace of 6th Dalai Lama Tsangyang Gyatso

name: Sela Pass
description: High-altitude mountain pass at 4,170 m on the border of Tawang and West Kameng districts. Key gateway on NH-13 with snow cover much of the year, Sela Lake nearby, and the recently opened Sela Tunnel below for all-weather access. Iconic scenic stop en route to Tawang.
facts: On border of Tawang and West Kameng
Sela Tunnel opened 2024 for all-weather connectivity

name: Nuranang Falls (Jang Falls)
description: 100 m high curtain waterfall near Jang town, originating from slopes of Sela Pass. Popular picnic and photography spot with a small hydel plant at the base. Featured in Bollywood films; named after a local Monpa legend.
facts: Near Jang town, ~40 km from Tawang
Also known as Bong Bong or Jung Falls

name: Sangetsar Tso (Madhuri Lake)
description: High-altitude lake at about 3,708 m formed by an earthquake, famous for partially submerged tree trunks in turquoise waters. Popularly called Madhuri Lake after a Bollywood song sequence. Located on the road toward Bum La Pass; requires permit and good weather for access.
facts: Formed by earthquake (trees still standing in water)
Army permit often required with Bum La route

name: Tawang War Memorial
description: Stupa-shaped memorial (about 12 m high) dedicated to Indian soldiers who died in the 1962 Sino-Indian War. Features engraved names, artifacts, and a peaceful hilltop setting with views over Tawang. Also known as Namgyal Chorten.

name: Pankang Teng Tso (PT Tso)
description: Pristine high-altitude lake about 17 km from Tawang in the Nagula wetland area, surrounded by rhododendron and pine. Freezes in winter; popular stop on the way to Bum La or Madhuri Lake. Spiritual significance in local Buddhist tradition.
facts: Often combined with Sangetsar Tso visit

name: Jaswant Garh War Memorial
description: Memorial honoring Rifleman Jaswant Singh Rawat of the 4th Garhwal Rifles for his bravery in the 1962 Sino-Indian War near Nuranang. Maintained site with flags and tributes along the highway between Sela and Tawang.
facts: Honors Rifleman Jaswant Singh Rawat MVC (posthumous)

name: Gorsam Chorten
description: Historic stupa near Zemithang in western Tawang district, significant in Monpa Buddhist tradition. Part of the offbeat Zemithang circuit with valley views and cultural importance.
facts: Near Zemithang village, ~85-90 km from Tawang
Part of western Tawang offbeat circuit
Accessible with ILP, no extra army permit typically
